LESSON: FOOTBALL

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.8: Football
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Football, part of Creating and Performing in Grade 7 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How can colours be used to show distance? 2. Why is ball control important in a football match?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. execute trapping skill in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform dribbling skill in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. execute shooting skill in football,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make improvised crayons for drawing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Football in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. create a pictorial composition using crayon etching inspired by football game,

   Football helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. value team effort in a football game and crayon etched drawing.

   Football helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch a virtual or live football demonstration of trapping skill: foot, thigh and chest, dribbling skill: inside and outside of the foot and shooting: low drive and placed shot,

2. demonstrate foot, thigh and chest trapping in football,

3. practise the trapping skills in football,

4. demonstrate dribbling skills in football using the inside and outside of the foot,

5. practise the dribbling skills in football game,

6. demonstrate low drive and placed shot in football,

7. practise shooting in football using low drive and placed shot,

8. play a mini football match or game while ensuring the learnt 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch a virtual or live football demonstration of trapping skill: foot, thigh and chest, dribbling skill: inside and outside of the foot and shooting: low drive and placed shot,
2. demonstrate foot, thigh and chest trapping in football,
3. practise the trapping skills in football,
4. demonstrate dribbling skills in football using the inside and outside of the foot,
5. practise the dribbling skills in football game,
6. demonstrate low drive and placed shot in football,
7. practise shooting in football using low drive and placed shot,
8. play a mini football match or game while ensuring the learnt 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Football together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and imagination: learner applies crayon to fill the paper in varied patterns, shapes or colour.

● Learning to Learn: the learner acquires and refines new skills in practising football.

● Self-Efficacy: Performing trapping, dribbling and shooting skills contributes to self-confidence as the learner showcases their

ability to execute fundamental football skills.

24

Values:
● Responsibility: as the learner paints a landscape composition of a football field, they take ownership of creating a visually

appealing representation and ensuring a clean working environment.

● Unity: as the learner performs football skills, they contribute to a positive and cooperative atmosphere, emphasising the

importance of working together.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Physical fitness: as the learner keeps fit while playing football for promotion of a healthy lifestyle.

● Friendship formation and interpersonal relationship: as the learner interacts and makes new friends during play.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Mathematics: Dribbling and shooting involves quick calculations of distances and angles. The learner applies mathematical

concepts to determine the most efficient paths and angles during dribbling, reinforcing practical mathematical application.
